Good Katy web design starts with a map, not a color scheme. The City of Katy counted 21,894 people in the 2020 census. The Katy school district counts more than 90,000 students. Those two numbers tell you most of what you need to know: the people who say "I live in Katy" mostly live outside the city, in master-planned communities spread across three counties, and they search by the name of their own community or the road they drive.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, a Texan who writes every page by hand from Big Sandy. He builds you a free demo first, and the price is printed: $497, $997 or $1,997, one time.

Katy web design for a place that crosses county lines

The Katy Area Economic Development Council describes the area as three counties and one marketplace. A Katy mailing address does not mean a home or shop is inside the City of Katy, and much of the area east of the city sits in unincorporated land or in Houston's extraterritorial jurisdiction.

  • Cinco RanchA master-planned community and census-designated place in Fort Bend and Harris counties, with 16,899 residents in the 2020 census.
  • Cross Creek RanchA 3,200-acre community with a Fulshear address, a reminder that some Katy-area customers live in another city entirely.
  • ElysonNorth of I-10 off the Grand Parkway near FM 529, a newer community between Katy and Cypress.
  • Old Town KatyThe historic downtown inside the city limits, where the Katy Rice Harvest Festival has been held each fall for decades.

Then come the roads everyone uses to give directions: I-10, the Grand Parkway, Fry Road and Mason Road. A homeowner in a newer section north of the freeway and one in an older section south of it may both say Katy, but they will not drive across the whole area for a haircut.

How to describe your service area when the address just says Katy

  1. Draw your real boundaryBefore anything is written, mark where you will actually go and where you will not. Honesty here saves wasted calls from across the county.
  2. Name communities, then roadsList the communities you serve, then the main roads that frame them. "South of I-10 between Fry and Mason" means something to a local.
  3. Give the busiest areas their own pageIf Cinco Ranch or Fulshear brings in a big share of your work, a page written for that place does more than a mention in a list.
  4. Keep the Google profile in stepYour Google Business Profile service area should match what the website says. Google weighs relevance, distance and prominence, and mixed signals help nobody.

Katy ISD households drive most of the demand

With more than 90,000 students spread over dozens of campuses, Katy ISD shapes the local economy. Busy families keep air conditioning crews, pool and lawn services, roofers, pediatric dentists, music teachers, sports coaches and tutors on their phones.

Those parents usually search at odd hours, after practice or after the kids are asleep, and they compare a few businesses side by side. The site that states its service area, hours and prices or estimate process plainly is the one that gets the call in the morning.

Growth has also slowed. Community Impact reported that enrollment growth has been slower since the 2024 to 2025 school year, and a late 2025 demographic study projected a small net decrease for the current year. For a small business, that means competition for the same households is getting tighter, not looser, and clear pages matter more.

Old Town Katy and the businesses along the freeway

The rice festival is a good reminder of where Katy came from. It began in the late 1970s or early 1980s as a "Sellabration" honoring the rice farming that once ran the local economy, and it moved into downtown Katy as crowds grew.

Shops, restaurants and salons in Old Town compete on charm and foot traffic. Offices along I-10 and the Grand Parkway, such as law firms, insurance agencies and accountants, compete on credibility. Each needs a different first page: one shows the place and the hours, the other shows the people and their qualifications.

Free and low-cost business help in the Katy area

Katy Area Economic Development Council

A private nonprofit that works to recruit, keep and grow businesses, and advises early-stage businesses on planning, site selection and financing.

Fort Bend County SBDC

Part of the University of Houston SBDC network, offering free, confidential one-on-one advising. Its Richmond office serves owners in Fort Bend County and southwest Harris County.

The Katy Area Chamber of Commerce is the other name owners hear often, for networking and member events. Dominion Web Design Pro has no relationship with any of these groups.

Choosing a package for a web design Katy TX business

A single storefront in Old Town or a small office off Mason Road usually fits Starter: $497 for five hand-written pages, including one about your service area, live in 7 to 14 days. Common questions

Where is Katy located in Texas?

Katy is west of Houston along Interstate 10, the Katy Freeway. The small City of Katy sits where Harris, Fort Bend and Waller counties meet, and the wider Katy area spreads mostly east of it through unincorporated communities, parts of Houston and parts of Fulshear. That is why one Katy address can mean very different places.

How much does web design in Katy, TX cost?

Prices vary a lot between freelancers, agencies and monthly site plans. Ours are printed and paid once: Starter $497 for five pages, Pro $997, Agency $1,997. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent, which is $297 a month after its free trial. Whoever you talk to, ask for the whole first-year cost so you can compare.

Should my Katy website mention Cinco Ranch, Fulshear and the other communities?

If you really work there, yes. People search with the name they live in, so a page about your services in Cinco Ranch or Fulshear gives that search something to match. Mention only places you serve, and give each important one real details, not a list of names at the bottom of the page.

What makes a good Katy web site for a home service company?

A clear list of the communities and roads you cover, the services you offer, real photos of your crew, hours, how fast you can usually come out, and a phone number that works from a cell phone. Families comparing three companies at night want those answers without having to call first.

Do you have an office in Katy?
